NORTHUMBERLAND

Bamburgh

No ratings yet

Bamburgh is one of Northumberland's most recognisable coastal villages, where a magnificent castle, huge sandy beach and centuries of history come together in one unforgettable setting.

Set high above the Northumberland coast, Bamburgh is one of the county's most iconic places to visit. The village is dominated by Bamburgh Castle, perched dramatically on a rocky outcrop overlooking the sea, while Bamburgh Beach stretches away beneath the dunes. Explore the castle and its grounds, discover the story of Grace Darling, wander through the village, or simply walk the beach with views towards Holy Island and the Farne Islands. There are also cafés, pubs, shops and family-friendly attractions, making Bamburgh an easy place to spend anything from a couple of hours to a full day.

HIGHLIGHTS

Things to see & do

Bamburgh Walled Garden

Bamburgh Walled Garden is a beautiful historic garden beside Bamburgh Castle, featuring colourful flower beds, mature trees and peaceful paths. It’s a lovely place to explore and enjoy a quieter side of Bamburgh.

Bamburgh Castle

Explore one of Northumberland's most spectacular castles, perched dramatically above the coastline. Discover royal history, impressive state rooms, ancient artefacts and sweeping views across the North Sea.

Bamburgh Beach

Walk the wide sweep of golden sand beneath Bamburgh Castle, with huge views across the North Sea towards the Farne Islands and Holy Island. It's perfect for a coastal walk, fresh air and spectacular photographs.

WHERE IS IT?

GETTING THERE

Bamburgh is easiest to reach by car via the A1. From the north, leave the A1 at Adderstone Services and follow the B1341 towards the coast. From the south, leave the A1 at Alnwick and follow the B1340 or B1342 towards Bamburgh. Buses also serve the village from surrounding towns including Alnwick and Berwick-upon-Tweed.

AT A GLANCE

Good to know

ADDRESS

Bamburgh, Northumberland
NE69 7AE

PARKING

Parking is available at Bamburgh Village Car Park opposite the castle, Bamburgh Castle Links Car Park, the seasonal Glebe Field near St Aidan's Church and other locations around the village. Castle parking is reserved for castle visitors. Parking can become busy during peak periods, so arriving early is recommended.

BEST TIME TO VISIT

Spring and summer offer the best chance of enjoying the beach, dunes and coastal walks, while early mornings and later afternoons can be quieter. Bamburgh is also worth visiting outside the main season, when the village and coastline take on a much wilder feel.

DOG FRIENDLY

Yes – dogs are welcome on Bamburgh Beach and in many outdoor areas, although individual attractions have their own restrictions. Bamburgh Castle allows dogs in its grounds, while some indoor attractions do not.

FAMILY FRIENDLY

Excellent – the beach, castle, playgrounds, museums, cafés and wide open spaces make Bamburgh a great choice for families.

ACCESSIBILITY

Good – accessible facilities are available at several locations. Bamburgh Walled Garden provides step-free access and a Changing Places Toilet. Some parts of Bamburgh Castle have steep paths, although accessible parking and a shuttle service are available.

TOILETS

Public toilets are available in the village, with additional facilities at Bamburgh Castle and other attractions.

OPENING HOURS

Bamburgh village and beach are accessible year-round. Individual attractions and businesses have their own opening hours, so check before travelling.
